title: The stalk of a colimit of sheaves of sets is the colimit of the stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $I$ a small category and $(\mathcal F_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of sheaves of sets on $X$ (sheaves on the site of open subsets of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]) with colimit $(\mathcal F,(c_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F)_i)$ in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For a presheaf of sets $\mathcal P$ on $X$ and $x\in X$ let $\mathcal P_x=\varinjlim_{U\ni x}\mathcal P(U)$ be its stalk (colimit of sets over the open neighbourhoods of $x$ ordered by reverse inclusion, with germs $s\mapsto s_x$), and for a morphism $\varphi$ let $\varphi_x$ be the map with $\varphi_x(s_x)=(\varphi_U(s))_x$. Then for every $x\in X$, $(\mathcal F_x,((c_i)_x)_i)$ is a colimit of the diagram of sets $(\mathcal F_{i,x})_{i\in I}$. In particular the stalk of a coproduct of sheaves of sets is the disjoint union of the stalks, and the stalk of a coequalizer $q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal F$ of $r,s:\mathcal D\rightrightarrows\mathcal C$ is the coequalizer of $r_x,s_x$, so $q_x$ is surjective.

source.place: Sheaves, Section Tag 009E (label section-limits-sheaves, line 3400), item (5): '(colim_i F_i)_x = colim_i F_{i,x}' ('The proofs are all easy')

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: for X : TopCat.{u} and C = Type u (which has colimits), stalkSkyscraperSheafAdjunction p₀ (Skyscraper.lean:402) makes Sheaf.forget (Type u) X ⋙ Presheaf.stalkFunctor (Type u) p₀ a left adjoint, so it preserves all colimits by Adjunction.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Limits.lean:92); TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (Stalks.lean:82) is the colimit over the open neighbourhoods and the map on stalks sends germs to germs (stalkFunctor_map_germ). The two special cases are the colimit of a discrete diagram and of a parallel pair in Type, where a coequalizer is a quotient set.
